tb-401-4.question:
Figure b shows the electric field established by two point charges.

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) If a charge is released from rest at P, it will move along the orange field line.

(2) If a charge is released from rest at Q, it will move along the violet field line.

(3) If a charge is released from rest at R, it will not move.

A (1) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-401-4.reasoning:
If a charge is released from rest at P, the direction of acceleration does not change throughout the motion.

∴ (1) is correct.

If a charge is released from rest at Q, it will experience an electrostatic force along the tangent to the field line. It leaves the field line once it starts moving.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

The electric field strength at R is not zero.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-401-6.question:
A particle of charge +q and mass m is released from rest between two horizontal metal plates (Fig d). The voltage across the plates is V and the distance between the plates is d. The acceleration due to gravity is g. What is the acceleration of the particle?

A g+Vqdm

B g+Vd

C g−Vqdm

D g−Vd
tb-401-6.reasoning:
The electric field between the plates points downwards. The electric force acting on the particle points downwards.

By E=FQ and E=Vd,

Fq =Vd

F =Vqd

By Fnet = ma,

F + W = ma

Vqd+ mg = ma

a = g +Vqdm

tb-401-7.question:
Particles X and Y enter an electric field set up by two parallel charged plates in turn at the same speed. The particles have the same mass and size but carry different charges. Their paths are shown in Figure e. Ignore the effect of gravity.

Which of the following statements about the particles is/are correct?

(1) X carries a positive charge.

(2) Y experiences a larger electric force than X.

(3) X carries a larger amount of charge than Y.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-401-7.reasoning:
X is attracted to the negative plate, so it carries positive charge.

∴ (1) is correct.

Y has a larger acceleration towards the plates. Since X and Y have the same mass, by F = ma, Y experiences a larger electric force than X.

∴ (2) is correct.

The electric field between the plates is uniform. By F = qE, the quantity of charge on Y is larger than that on X.

∴ (3) is incorrect.

tb-401-8.question:
Two small spheres X and Y are suspended by identical insulating string from the same point. They repel each other. At equilibrium, X is at a higher position than Y (Fig f).

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(1) The force acting on X by Y is larger in magnitude than the force on Y by X.

(2) X may be neutral.

(3) The mass of Y is larger than that of X.

A (1) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (2) and (3) only
tb-401-8.reasoning:
The force acting on X by Y and the force on Y by X form an action-and-reaction pair, so they are equal in magnitude.

∴ (1) is incorrect.

X and Y must carry the same kind of charge as they repel each other.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

Let θX be the angle between the vertical and the string suspending X.

Let F be the magnitude of horizontal component of the electrostatic force between X and Y.

tan θX =FmXg

Let θY be the angle between the vertical and the string suspending Y.

tan θY =FmYg

Since θX > θY, mY > mX.

∴ (3) is correct.

tb-401-10.question:
In Figure g, point charges Q1 (+5 × 10−8 C) and Q2 (−5 × 10−8 C) are 40 cm and 50 cm from point O respectively.

Which arrow gives the possible direction of the resultant electric field at O?

A Arrow w

B Arrow x

C Arrow y

D Arrow z
tb-401-10.reasoning:
The electric field produced at O by the two charges are as shown.

Consider the vertical direction.

The vertical component of E1 points downwards and that of E2 is zero. Therefore, the vertical component of the resultant field must point downwards.

∴ w is not possible.

Consider the horizontal direction.

Since E2 points to the left, the resultant field must not point to the right of E1.

∴ z is not possible.

Consider the direction perpendicular to L.

Since Q1 and Q2 carries the same quantity of charge and Q1 is closer to O than Q2, the magnitude of E1 is larger than that of E2.

Therefore, the component of resultant electric field perpendicular to L must point to the right of L.

∴ x is not possible.

tb-401-11.question:
Two positive point charges Q1 and Q2 are 4 cm apart, both lying on a straight line L (Fig h). The amount of charge carried by Q1 is larger than that carried by Q2.

Which of the following graphs best describes the resultant electric field strength E at different points on L between Q1 and Q2? Take the direction to the right as positive and d as the distance from Q1.
tb-401-11.reasoning:
In the region between Q1 and Q2, Q1 produces an electric field pointing to the right and Q2 produces an electric field pointing to the left.

Therefore, the resultant electric field points to the right at a position near Q1 and points to the left at a position near Q2.

∴ B and D are incorrect.

Since the quantity of charge carried by Q1 is larger than that carried by Q2, the neutral point is closer to Q2 than to Q1.

∴ A is incorrect.

tb-401-12.question:
Point charges Q1 and Q2 are fixed on a straight line passing through points X and Y (Fig i). The resultant electric field due to Q1 and Q2 points left at X and points right at Y. Which of the following statements are correct?

(1) The resultant electric field strength is zero somewhere along line XY.

(2) Q1 is a positive charge and Q2 a negative charge.

(3) Q2 is greater in charge quantity than Q1.

A (1) and (2) only

B (1) and (3) only

C (2) and (3) only

D (1), (2) and (3)
tb-401-12.reasoning:
The resultant electric field change direction somewhere between X and Y. There must be a neutral point between X and Y.

∴ (1) is correct.

If the charge quantity of Q1 is greater than or equal to that of Q2, in region to the left of Q1, E1 must be larger than E2 and the resultant field would not change direction. Therefore, Q2 must be greater in charge quantity than Q1.

∴ (3) is correct.

Consider the region to the left of Q1.

If Q1 is positive and Q2 is negative, the resultant field would point to the left at a position near Q1 and point to the right at a position far from Q1.

∴ (2) is incorrect.

tb-401-13.question:
X and Y are two identical small metal spheres. The amount of charges carried by X and Y are in the ratio 1 : 3 but the type of charges carried by each sphere is unknown. The electrostatic force between them is F. X is brought to touch Y and is placed back to its original position afterwards. Which of the following give(s) the possible magnitude of the electrostatic force between X and Y after they touch?

(1) F3 (2) 4F3 (3) 4F

A (2) only

B (3) only

C (1) and (2) only

D (1) and (3) only
tb-401-13.reasoning:
Suppose X initially carries charge Q. Then Y carries 3Q or –3Q.

Before touching, the electrostatic force between them has magnitude F =3Q24πε0d2 where d is the distance between them.

After touching, they may both carry 2Q or –Q. The magnitude of electrostatic force between them are 4Q24πε0d2=4F3 and Q24πε0d2=F3 respectively in these two cases.

tb-401-24.question:
Read the following passage about pulsed electric field process and answer the questions that follow.

The pulsed electric field (PEF) process can improve the quality of potato chips. In this process, potatoes are put between two metal plates. (a) Besides increasing the voltage, suggest another way that can increase the electric field strength between the two metal plates. (1 mark)

tb-401-24.answer:
(a) Reduce the separation between the plates.

1A
